title: Network-AI MCP SSE server -- T1190 empty-default-secret always-authorized bypass
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-48814 (GHSA-r78r-rwrf-rjwp, CVSS
9.1 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory for Network-AI, a TypeScript/
Node.js multi-agent orchestrator.

This is a "the previous fix was incomplete" case: an earlier advisory
(CVE-2026-46701, fixed in 5.4.5) closed a CORS flaw by restricting
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to localhost origins, but the DEEPER bug
survived that fix untouched. The SSE MCP server's secret defaults to an
empty string (`secret: process.env['NETWORK_AI_MCP_SECRET'] ?? ''`), and
the authorization check itself treats an empty secret as "always
authorized" (`if (!this._opts.secret) return true;`). A non-loopback bind
still only logged a warning rather than refusing to start. The CORS fix
only stops a BROWSER from making the request cross-origin -- it does
nothing for curl, SSRF, or any other non-browser caller reaching a
`0.0.0.0` bind directly, so all 22 MCP tools (`config_set`, `agent_spawn`,
`blackboard_write`, `token_*`, and others) remained invocable with zero
credentials.

This corpus already carries two other unauthenticated-MCP-endpoint rules
under T1190 (`observed_ruflo_mcp_bridge_unauth_terminal_execute_t1190`,
`observed_mcp_pinot_unauth_confused_deputy_t1190`); this one is
mechanistically distinct from both -- not a missing check (Ruflo) and
not a working-but-off-by-default toggle (mcp-pinot), but a check that
LOOKS present in the code yet is logically a no-op whenever its own
configuration default is used.

Detection logic flags a `tools/call` JSON-RPC request against one of the
higher-privilege tool names, arriving with no `secret`/bearer credential
field at all -- the empty-secret failure mode means "credential absent"
and "credential present but wrong" are NOT equivalent signals here; only
the former exploits this specific bug.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (Jovancoding, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 5.7.2.
